findings.claim: In concatenatedRSToASN1DER, lines 114-115 call ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger) and ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger) and discard the results. The return statement at lines 117-121 repeats the encoding with new encoders, so lines 114-115 are dead code.

CryptoIntegration.detectProvider() no longer throws the fail-fast 'Multiple crypto providers loaded' IllegalStateException; it picks the highest order() instead. The Default, Elytron and FIPS1402 providers all return 200, so a tie is decided by ServiceLoader/classpath order. For example, a FIPS deployment with a stray crypto-default jar can run on non-FIPS BouncyCastle without failing.
concatenatedRSToASN1DER() assumes signature.length == signLength without validating it. A malformed signature can throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException instead of IOException.
